title: Regional Restrictions and Exceptions
prompt: You want to centrally deny resource creation in unapproved Regions across an organization's member accounts while preserving the operations required for global services.

choices.text: Use AWS Config to detect unapproved Regions.
choices.explanation: This detects activity after the fact and does not deny creation requests.

choices.text: Use an SCP with conditions such as aws:RequestedRegion to deny access, and exempt the actions required for global services.
choices.explanation: An SCP can be applied across the organization as a boundary on IAM permissions.

choices.text: Manually create IAM groups for users in each account.
choices.explanation: This does not centrally control other principals that may be created in member accounts.

learning.reason: An SCP can be applied across the organization as a boundary on IAM permissions.
learning.concept: An SCP does not grant permissions. Review global service APIs and cross-Region side effects as well.

title: Keeping Writes in Sync During Migration
prompt: You are migrating a corresponding on-premises database to AWS. You want to perform an initial full load and replicate writes until just before cutover.

choices.text: Combine a full load with CDC in AWS DMS.
choices.explanation: Source changes can continue to be replicated after the initial transfer.
Changes made after the snapshot is taken are not replicated automatically.

choices.text: Switch to the new database and then copy the old database's configuration.
choices.explanation: This does not transfer the data or the latest changes.

learning.reason: Source changes can continue to be replicated after the initial transfer.
learning.concept: Check CDC latency and the source database's logging settings, and validate that the remaining changes are consistent before cutover.

title: Hybrid DNS
prompt: You need to resolve a Route 53 private hosted zone name in a VPC from an on-premises network. What should you use when the VPC is reachable over a VPN?

choices.text: Put the private records in the on-premises public DNS.
choices.explanation: This would expose the names publicly and would not resolve them through the private hosted zone.

choices.text: Create only a Resolver outbound endpoint.
choices.explanation: It is used for queries sent from the VPC to external DNS servers.

choices.text: Configure conditional forwarding from the corporate DNS server to a Resolver inbound endpoint.
choices.explanation: This sends on-premises queries to the VPC-side Resolver.

learning.reason: This sends on-premises queries to the VPC-side Resolver.
learning.concept: Read inbound and outbound from the VPC-side Resolver's perspective. DNS forwarding ports and routing are also required.

category: 組織横断の設計、移行、複雑な構成
title: Choosing a Warm Standby Strategy
prompt: You want to keep costs at the DR site low while maintaining a small environment there before a failure, scaling it up during an outage, and cutting over quickly using a tested procedure. Which strategy should you choose?

choices.explanation: This does not keep the DR site scaled down and waiting in order to reduce overall costs.
The DR site is restored and prepared to run after the failure.
A scaled-down version of the application and data is maintained at the DR site and scaled up when needed.

learning.reason: A scaled-down version of the application and data is maintained at the DR site and scaled up when needed.
learning.concept: RTO is the target recovery time; RPO is the acceptable time window for data loss. Even with the same strategy, measure replication and failover in practice.

title: Separating Accounts
prompt: You want to manage your production and development accounts as an organization and avoid having staff manage long-term IAM users individually.

choices.text: Share the production root user's access keys among all staff
choices.explanation: This prevents auditing and managing permissions per person and relies on long-term credentials.

choices.text: Manage account assignments and permission sets with IAM Identity Center
choices.explanation: You can assign users or groups temporary access to multiple accounts.

choices.text: Manually create IAM users with the same name in every account
choices.explanation: Managing long-term credentials separately in each account would continue.

learning.reason: You can assign users or groups temporary access to multiple accounts.
learning.concept: Design centralized authentication and least privilege for each account separately.

category: 組織横断の設計、移行、複雑な構成
title: Connecting to a Service with Overlapping Addresses
prompt: You want to let two VPCs with overlapping CIDRs use only a specific TCP service behind the provider's NLB.

choices.text: Use an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service
choices.explanation: This creates an entry point to the service for consumers without routing the entire provider VPC.

choices.text: Peer the VPCs while keeping their CIDRs overlapping
choices.explanation: VPCs with overlapping CIDRs cannot be peered.

choices.text: Propagate every VPC route to a TGW as-is in both directions
choices.explanation: Overlapping address ranges cannot be distinguished at the same time.

learning.reason: This creates an entry point to the service for consumers without routing the entire provider VPC.
learning.concept: Service-level exposure and network-to-network connectivity are different requirements. PrivateLink is an option for private connectivity to a single service.
